preconditions.expression: all(line.strip() == '' or (line.strip().isdigit() and 1 <= int(line.strip()) <= 500000) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() != '')
preconditions.description: The first line is a positive integer (number of test cases) between 1 and 500,000. Empty lines separate test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(test_case) == 2 for test_case in [input.splitlines()[i:i+2] for i in range(1, len(input.splitlines()), 3) if i+1 < len(input.splitlines())])
preconditions.description: Each test case consists of exactly two non-empty lines: the first is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 500,000), and the second is a string of length n with characters 'V', 'K', or '?'

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == int(n) for n, s in [input.splitlines()[i:i+2] for i in range(1, len(input.splitlines()), 3) if i+1 < len(input.splitlines())])
preconditions.description: The length of the string matches the integer n provided in the test case.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in {'V', 'K', '?'} for c in s) for n, s in [input.splitlines()[i:i+2] for i in range(1, len(input.splitlines()), 3) if i+1 < len(input.splitlines())])
preconditions.description: The string consists only of characters 'V', 'K', or '?'

postconditions.description: For each test case, exactly two lines of output are produced: the first line is the count of possible periods, and the second line lists the periods in increasing order.

postconditions.expression: all(len(periods) == int(count) for count, periods in zip(output_lines[::2], output_lines[1::2]))
postconditions.description: The number of periods listed matches the count provided in the preceding line.

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= d <= n for d in map(int, periods.split())) for n, _, periods in zip(test_cases_n, test_cases_s, output_lines[1::2]))
postconditions.description: Each period d is an integer between 1 and the length of the string n.

postconditions.expression: all(all(d1 <= d2 for d1, d2 in zip(periods.split(), periods.split()[1:])) for periods in output_lines[1::2])
postconditions.description: The periods are listed in strictly increasing order.

postconditions.expression: all(set(map(int, periods.split())) == set(d for d in range(1, n+1) if all(s[(i + d) % n] == s[i] or s[(i + d) % n] == '?' or s[i] == '?' for i in range(n))) for n, s, periods in zip(test_cases_n, test_cases_s, output_lines[1::2]))
postconditions.description: The set of periods is exactly the set of integers d (1 ≤ d ≤ n) such that for every possible replacement of '?' with 'V' or 'K', the string has period d. This means for every position i, s[i] and s[(i + d) % n] are either equal or at least one of them is '?' (so they can be made equal by replacement).
